scraped.title: Benchlearning among Public Employment Services
scraped.subtitle: Benchlearning among the Public Employment Services (PES) in the Western Balkans Six (WB6)
scraped.description: The project “Benchlearning among the Public Employment Services in the Western Balkans Six” supports Public Employment Services in the region to improve their performance, organisational capacity and quality of services for jobseekers, workers and employers.
body: The project “Benchlearning among the Public Employment Services in the Western Balkans Six” supports Public Employment Services in the region to improve their performance, organisational capacity and quality of services for jobseekers, workers and employers.

The project is implemented as part of ESAP 3, within the broader EU4Employment Action, financed by the European Union through the Instrument for Pre-accession Assistance (IPA III). ESAP 3 promotes fair and well-functioning labour markets in the Western Balkans, in line with the European Pillar of Social Rights.

The project helps Public Employment Services become more effective, responsive, inclusive and resilient. This is achieved through a structured process of self-assessment, peer exchange, mutual learning, performance analysis and evidence-based action planning. The aim is not to rank PES systems, but to support practical learning and continuous improvement.

A central objective is to bring the WB6 Benchlearning methodology closer to the approach used at European level, while adapting it to the institutional and operational context of the Western Balkans Six. The process combines quantitative data, such as harmonised administrative indicators, with qualitative evidence gathered through self-assessment, peer reviews, group discussions and internal PES documents.

ICON is contracted to provide technical assistance by preparing the methodology, indicators, data collection templates, qualitative assessment tools and questionnaires on digitalisation and the green transition. During implementation, participating public employment services carry out self-assessments and peer reviews, supported by analysis of both data and institutional evidence. Where feasible, practitioners from European public employment services contribute to mutual learning activities.

The final phase focuses on sharing results, identifying good practices, organising thematic exchanges and supporting future action planning. A study visit, workshops and a final event will help translate findings into practical improvements.

ICON’s support includes methodological guidance, training of local experts, harmonisation of administrative data, facilitation of peer learning, data analysis, thematic surveys, preparation of a WB6 PES Benchlearning Practitioner’s Guide, supervision of WB6-specific reports and production of a regional comparative report.
